literal: A toṭi measure of dust to become a kaḵcu measure if dried, handful of even manure without needing, abundantly it will yield.
translation: If plowed soil is left to dry until a full measure of dust shrinks to a quarter, the field will yield abundantly without needing even a handful of manure.
modern: ஒரு தொடி அளவுள்ள உழுத மண்ணானது கஃசு அளவாகக் குறையும்படி நன்றாகக் காயவிட்டால், ஒரு பிடி எருவும் தேவையில்லாமல் நிலம் மிகுதியாக விளைச்சலைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of properly drying and aerating plowed soil before sowing. The poet uses two traditional weights to illustrate this: 'toṭi' (a larger measure) and 'kaḵcu' (a smaller measure, a quarter of a toṭi). If the soil is turned to dust and dried in the sun until its weight reduces from a toṭi to a kaḵcu, it becomes highly fertile. Under such well-prepared conditions, the field will yield an abundant harvest without requiring even a single handful of manure.
